figures.label: S2
figures.caption: Figure S2. The peak area ratio of different Li+-coordinating complexes in the CPME and CPME/THF electrolytes as calculated from Raman spectra. In Figure S2, the TFSI⁻ anion exhibits three characteristic vibrational bands corresponding to solvent-separated ion pairs (SSIP, ~736 cm−1), contact ion pairs (CIP, ~742 cm−1), and higher aggregates (AGG, ~748 cm−1). The CPME based electrolytes are dominated by CIP/AGG species, which favor the formation of anion-derived interfacial films. Relative to pure CPME, the CPME/THF electrolyte exhibits a lower AGG fraction and a higher CIP fraction, giving smaller Li⁺–salt clusters with higher mobility under an electric field.

figures.label: S10
figures.caption: Figure S10. In-situ EIS measurements and corresponding GITT curves (a) equivalent circuit, (b, e) CPME, (c, f) CPME/THF, and (d, g) CPME/THF 1:1 electrolyte. In-situ EIS was conducted to evaluate the interfacial charge-transfer behavior of Li–S cells with different electrolytes during cycling. The Nyquist plots exhibit two main semicircles at high frequency, representing the interphase contact resistance (R2) of the surface of sulfur cathodes, and the charge transfer resistance (R3). Additionally, a short sloping tail at low frequency corresponds to the Warburg impedance (Q4). The CPME/THF electrolyte exhibited relatively low and stable impedance throughout both the discharge and charge processes, indicating efficient Li⁺ transport and fast interfacial charge transfer. In contrast, the CPME electrolyte showed a much higher interfacial resistance, suggesting sluggish reaction kinetics. Mo

figures.label: S12
figures.caption: Figure S12. The SEM images and EDS mapping of Li2S deposition on the CP current collector for the S8@CP−Li cell in (a, b) CPME, (c, d) CPME/THF electrolyte. In Figure S12, the discharged cathode from the CPME/THF electrolyte exhibits a more uniform distribution of sulfur-containing discharge products, while the CPME electrode shows a less homogeneous deposition feature. The corresponding sulfur elemental mapping further reveals a more evenly distributed sulfur signal across the cathode surface in CPME/THF, suggesting a more uniform redistribution of sulfur-containing discharge products during discharge. These results provide evidence that the CPME/THF electrolyte promotes a more homogeneous Li2S deposition process, which is consistent with the improved sulfur utilization observed in electrochemical measurements.

figures.caption: Figure S15. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further reveal that the adsorption energies of CPME molecules on the β-S8 (130), (300), and (–221) planes. The (130) plane exhibits the lowest adsorption energy, indicating that CPME preferentially adsorbs on this surface, slowing its growth rate and promoting its exposure. This facet-selective interaction suggests that CPME facilitates nucleation and growth along the (130) plane of β-S8, ultimately regulating sulfur crystallographic orientation during charge recovery.
